chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

It should be buried and not sold. The proper way regarding these two reports is that we carry them upon a kind of recommendation. It is also possible that what is intended by the two reports is water whose one of whose qualities has changed, while the first two reports concern well-water, whose ruling is not that, and which can be purified by drawing out water, because that is a lighter impurity than water changed by najasah.

key_terms.الْمَاءَ: the water under discussion in the ruling
key_terms.بِالنَّزْحِ: by drawing out water from the well

ai.seo_question: How do Shia scholars reconcile hadith about impure water used in dough or other mixtures?
ai.summary: This passage discusses reconciling reports about impure water used in dough and similar matters. It explains that some reports may be understood as indicating recommendation, or as referring specifically to water whose properties have changed through najasah, in contrast to well-water that may be purified by drawing water from it.
